title: The influence of menstrual cycle phases on neuromuscular knee joint coordination in female footballers: a prospective observational study
summary: Knee injuries occur more frequently in female football players than in male players. Hormonal changes during the menstrual cycle are thought to influence how muscles work together and how stable the knee joint is during sporting movements. However, it is still unclear whether these cycle-related changes can be observed during simple functional movement tests. The aim of this study is therefore to investigate whether balance performance and muscle activity of the lower limb differ across different phases of the menstrual cycle in female football players. Healthy female football players perform a standardized single-leg balance test at several time points during their menstrual cycle. During the test, the reaching distance of the free leg in different directions is recorded. At the same time, muscle activity of selected leg and hip muscles is measured using sensors attached to the skin. No training, treatment, or intervention is applied.
conditions: Investigation of cycle-related differences in functional knee stability and muscle activity in healthy female football players.

interventions.name: Healthy female football players with a regular menstrual cycle. Participants are enrolled in a prospective, non-interventional observational study with repeated assessments over time. No intervention is applied.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Active player in a professional soccer club (at least two training sessions per week)
• Regular cycle (approx. 25–35 days) in the last three months
• Written consent (if < 18 years of age, additional consent from legal guardian required)
Exclusion criteria:
- Use of hormonal contraceptives (oral preparations, hormonal IUD, implant, depot preparations, etc.)
- Condition following clinically relevant knee injury (e.g., anterior cruciate ligament ruptures, complex muscle lesions, collateral ligament ruptures)
- Current or recent (≤ 6 months) injury or surgery of the lower extremity.
- Intercurrent injury to the lower extremity during the study period that prevents safe participation in the YBT/sEMG
- Known endocrine disorders (e.g., thyroid disorders, polycystic ovary syndrome) or pronounced cycle dysregulation
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding
- Lack of capacity to give consent
